summary: Before joining tables, know how they relate and what one row means. This is called the grain, and it prevents most join mistakes.
points: One-to-many means one row here links to many rows there: one customer has many orders.
The foreign key lives on the many side: orders stores customer_id.
The grain is what one row represents: one row of order_items is one product in one order.
To check a relationship, group by the key and count rows per value.

example.explanation: Some customers have several orders, which shows that customers to orders is one-to-many.
